author: Ari Koslow
title: Lucas Giolito takes loss Monday
desc: Lucas Giolito allowed three runs on seven hits over five innings in a bulk relief role with two strikeouts and three walks in a loss on Monday against the Cardinals.
impact: Giolito pitched behind an opener in Wandy Peralta who tossed a scoreless opening frame. Giolito has continued to struggle pitching deep into starts. He'll face the Rangers next.

author: David Leisering
title: Michael Lorenzen tosses second straight solid outing Monday
desc: Michael Lorenzen settled for a no-decision on Monday despite limiting the Cubs to one run on five hits over five innings. He walked one and struck out five.
impact: Lorenzen has now posted back-to-back strong outings - both against the Cubs - after a disastrous start to his season. He did allow a home run to Pete Crow-Armstrong in the bottom of the first, but otherwise it was another solid start from the veteran righthander. Over his last two outings, Lorenzen has allowed two runs on seven hits with a 12:3 K:BB ratio in 10 innings - lowering his season ERA from 8.01 to 7.13 in the process. He has, however, not won a game since April 24 against the Mets and has gone 0-6 with three no-decisions in his last nine starts. Still, Lorenzen's last two outings are a step in the right direction and he'll look to continue his turnaround on Sunday against the Pirates at Coors Field.

author: David Leisering
title: Cole Carrigg drives in all four runs in 5-4 loss to Cubs Monday
desc: Cole Carrigg went 1-for-3 with a three-run homer, a walk, and four RBI on Monday in the Rockies' 5-4 loss to the Cubs.
impact: Carrigg almost single-handedly won the game for the Rockies on Monday. He drew a bases-loaded walk in the sixth that tied the game at 1-1 and then hit a go-ahead, three-run shot in the eighth which gave the Rockies a 4-2 lead. Since his call-up to the majors on June 9, Carrigg has hit safely in five of his seven games and is batting .259 (7-for-27) with three home runs, six runs batted in, and a 1.000 OPS. It looks like Carrigg is going to get every opportunity to showcase his ability in the Rockies' lineup and definitely is worth a flier in deeper leagues with the way he has broken into the league.

author: David Leisering
title: Shota Imanaga extends winless streak to seven straight Monday
desc: Shota Imanaga went 5.2 innings on Monday and allowed one run on five hits, walked one, and struck out three in a no-decision against the Rockies.
impact: Despite the strong outing, Imanaga saw his winless streak reach seven straight starts as he has gone 0-4 since his last victory on May 7 against the Reds. After a four-start stretch that saw him allow 26 runs on 27 hits - including 12 home runs - in 21.2 innings, Imanaga seems to have righted the ship with his second consecutive solid outing. Despite only striking out three batters, Imanaga was not charged with a run until the sixth inning. He departed with the Cubs leading 1-0 and runners at first and second with two outs. However, reliever Phil Maton hit a batter to load the bases then walked in the tying run before getting out of the jam. Over his last two starts, Imanaga has given up one run on seven hits with a 10:3 K:BB ratio in 10.2 innings. He's lined up for a home start against the Blue Jays on Sunday.

author: David Leisering
title: Pete Crow-Armstrong hits for cycle in Monday victory
desc: Pete Crow-Armstrong had a perfect night at the plate, hitting for the league's first cycle of the 2026 season, as the Cubs defeated the Rockies, 5-4.
impact: Crow-Armstrong's cycle was the 13th in franchise history as was the first by a Cub since Carson Kelly accomplished the feat on March 31, 2025. It was the first cycle in the majors since Minnesota's Byron Buxton on July 12, 2025 and it was the 350th cycle in baseball history. Crow-Armstrong accomplished the cycle in rare fashion, doing it in reverse order to become the first player since Rajai Davis in 2016 to perform that trick. Crow-Armstrong started with a solo home run off of Colorado starter Michael Lorenzen to lead off the bottom of the first. It was his 13th blast of the season. He then tripled in the third, doubled in the fifth, and singled in the seventh to cap off the cycle. He added a sacrifice fly in the eighth for his second RBI of the night. Crow-Armstrong has hit safely in 18 of his last 19 games and is hitting a ridiculous .436 (24-for-55) with 10 runs scored, four doubles, two triples, six home runs, nine runs batted in, and four steals in 13 games this month. Over his last 19 games, Crow-Armstrong has raised his average from .223 to .277 and his OPS from .674 to .844. He is hands down the hottest hitter in the game right now.

author: Diego Sandoval
title: Trea Turner (wrist) leaves game early, X-rays come back negative
desc: Trea Turner had his X-rays come back negative after being hit by a pitch on the wrist on Monday against the Marlins.
impact: Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said that he expects Turner to be sore and they will see how he feels on Tuesday. The shortstop should be viewed as day-to-day until another update is provided.

author: Nate Miller
title: Gabriel Rincones hits first MLB home run Monday night
desc: Gabriel Rincones went 1-for-4 with a solo home run and two total RBI in Monday's 7-0 win over the Marlins.
impact: In just his second MLB game, Rincones hit the first big-league homer of his career Monday night, getting the Phillies out to an early lead in the second frame. The 25-year-old outfielder also drove in the Phillies' second run of the game with a fielder's choice in the third. Rincones could see a significant amount of at-bats with outfielder Adolis Garcia (lat) on the shelf.

author: Nate Miller
title: J.T. Realmuto rips two-run homer Monday night
desc: J.T. Realmuto went 1-for-4 with a two-run homer in Monday's 7-0 win over the Marlins.
impact: Realmuto has gotten locked in at the plate. The veteran backstop has homered in each of his last two games, going 4-for-8 with a walk and six RBI overall.

author: Nate Miller
title: Justin Crawford drives in a run, scores another Monday night
desc: Justin Crawford went 3-for-4 with three singles, one RBI, one run scored, and a steal in Monday's 7-0 win over the Marlins.
impact: After not starting the last two days, Crawford was back in center field for the Phillies on Monday. The rookie speedster had been batting just .214 with a weak .491 OPS over 29 plate appearances this month, but he got on track with a strong night. Crawford raised his average 10 points and swiped his ninth bag of the year

author: Nate Miller
title: Zack Wheeler dominates Marlins on Monday
desc: Zack Wheeler gave up just two hits and three walks while striking out nine across six shutout innings in Monday's 7-0 win against the Marlins.
impact: Wheeler has been in a serious groove since the calendar flipped to June. Through three starts this month, the ace righty has now put up a stellar 1.42 ERA and 0.84 WHIP with 22 strikeouts over 19 innings. He will to keep it rolling Sunday against the Mets.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Cal Raleigh (oblique) confirms he will be activated Tuesday
desc: Cal Raleigh told reporters he will be activated from the injured list on Tuesday.
impact: Raleigh will be back after concluding his rehab assignment over the weekend. He'll return from a month-long absence.

author: David Leisering
title: Eiberson Castellano optioned to Triple-A Albuquerque
desc: Eiberson Castellano has been optioned to Triple-A Albuquerque by the Colorado Rockies. The move was made as Victor Vodnik (elbow) was reinstated from the injured list.
impact: Castellano made his only appearance - and his major league debut - on Sunday in the Rockies' 23-9 win over the Athletics. He recorded a three-inning save, allowing no runs on four hits while striking out two. Castellano was having a solid season in the minors, posting a 2.44 ERA in 59 innings between Double-A Portland and Triple-A Albuquerque. It's likely Castellano will return to Colorado at some point later in the year.

author: David Leisering
title: Victor Vodnik (elbow) reinstated from injured list
desc: Victor Vodnik (elbow) has been reinstated from the 15-day injured list by the Colorado Rockies. In a corresponding move, Eiberson Castellano was optioned to Triple-A Albuquerque.
impact: Vodnik missed nearly a month of action, last appearing in a game on May 18 against the Rangers. The righthander struggled prior to his stint on the IL, going 1-2 with an 8.00 ERA, a 2.11 WHIP, and a 16:13 K:BB ratio in 18 innings. He pitched two scoreless innings during his rehab stint at Triple-A Albuquerque, walking one and striking out four. He'll have an opportunity to compete for saves again with the Rockies.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Walker Jenkins (shoulder) to join Single-A Cedar Rapids for rehab
desc: Walker Jenkins is continuing his rehab assignment with Single-A Cedar Rapids.
impact: Jenkins will continue on the next phase of his rehab. He continues to work his way back from a shoulder injury.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Brady Basso optioned to Triple-A
desc: The Athletics optioned Brady Basso to Triple-A Las Vegas.
impact: Basso will return to Triple-A after he was called up over the weekend. Luis Morales was recalled as the corresponding move.
